thread:
Anya Chen: quick follow-up from the autoscaler RFC — worried about duplicate intent application when control-plane and operator race. sketch below.
Anya Chen: TL;DR: make intents idempotent, attach versioned lease tokens, and use a short reconcile id to detect replays.
Mike Patel: Can you sketch the flow? worried about operator restart / double-apply.
Anya Chen: Flow idea: client -> control-plane writes Intent{uid, version, spec} -> control-plane annotates Pool with intentID (CAS) -> operator sees intent, tries to allocate -> operator writes Lease{intentID, leaseVersion, nodeSet} -> control-plane marks intent resolved once lease persisted. If operator retries, it compares leaseVersion and is idempotent.
Yuji Tanaka: How to prevent two operators taking same intent? CAS on pool annotation + leader-election isn't enough for edge cases.
Sophia Nguyen: use API server CAS (ResourceVersion) for the Pool annotation; operator does patch with expected resourceVersion. If patch fails, re-fetch. Also consider ephemeral LeaseClaim CRD: operator creates LeaseClaim CR; API server enforces single creator via finalizers.
Ethan Ross: extra CRD round trips add latency. Do we care for small claims (100ms) vs big prewarm ops?
Anya Chen: Agreed. We'll only create LeaseClaim for multi-node allocations or >threshold memory. For tiny prewarm (1-2 slots) operator can do optimistic local admission with eventual consistency.
Mike Patel: what about idempotency keys for client resends? need to tolerate control-plane retries too.
Anya Chen: Intent.uid is the dedupe key. control-plane increments intent.version on any spec change. operator stores lastObservedIntentVersion per pool. If incoming version <= lastObserved, operator treats as no-op.
Sophia Nguyen: also add a 2-phase commit window: operator reserves nodes for Xs, writes Lease with state=RESERVED, then transitions to ACTIVE after health checks. If operator crashes in RESERVED, a TTL cleans it up.
Yuji Tanaka: TTL semantics + garbage collection + admin override needed. GC should prefer oldest intents first.
Ethan Ross: what about admission fairness? tenants with reserved capacity shouldn't be starved by aggressive bursters.
Anya Chen: we'll track tenant credits separately and expose a soft admission policy: reserve quota, burst tokens, and preemption priority buckets. Policy arithmetic lives in control-plane; operator enforces admission decisions.
Anya Chen: minimal YAML sketch:
```yaml
# Intent (control-plane)
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: PoolIntent
metadata:
  uid: intent-12345
  version: "3"
spec:
  tenant: acme
  nodes: 4
  profile: gpu-rtx-small
---
# Lease (operator)
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: PoolLease
metadata:
  name: lease-12345
spec:
  intentUID: intent-12345
  leaseVersion: "1"
  nodes: [n1,n2,n3,n4]
  state: RESERVED
```
Sophia Nguyen: Nice. We should also expose metrics: intent_apply_attempts, lease_conflicts, lease_gc_count. Add tracing spans across control-plane -> apiserver -> operator.
Mike Patel: ops question: how to roll out the operator change safely? feature flag gated and staged in staging then canary in prod.
orchestrator-bot: deploy/orchestrator v2.3.1 promoted to staging at 2026-03-21T09:12:00Z :rocket:
Anya Chen: plan for rollout: 1) implement idempotent intent handling + lease CRD, 2) add GC + TTL, 3) gate via feature flag, 4) canary on low-traffic pools, 5) monitor lease_conflicts and intent_apply_attempts.
Ethan Ross: one more: telemetry for failed CAS vs conflict should be distinct so we can tell bad controller logic vs normal races.
Yuji Tanaka: I'll prototype a LeaseClaim CRD and a small controller to exercise the pattern this week.
Anya Chen: thanks! I'll update the RFC with the intent/lease diagram and the rollout checklist. :thumbsup:
